supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42:53 UTC, DC-RB-01 recorded cole.price being added to Remote Desktop Users, with dev.sharma as the subject account and subject logon ID 0x7a76dca.
The group-change logon ID matches a network logon to DC-RB-01 as dev.sharma from 10.60.10.22 at 13:40:15 UTC. This identifies the recorded account and source address, not the human operator.

The addition conflicts with the supplied restriction of Remote Desktop Users membership to IT: cole.price is identified as a vet tech. The scheduled Billing-Share change for hana.ito does not explain this different member and group. This makes the alerted change suspicious but does not establish malicious intent.

The alerted change originated through a session sourced from 10.60.10.22, whereas observed outbound traffic from WS-DSHARMA-01 used 10.60.10.23. The supplied records do not identify the host owning 10.60.10.22.

At 13:43:55 UTC, cole.price's UserAssist registry entry on WS-CPRICE-01 was updated for a ROT13-encoded path that decodes to C:\Windows\System32\mstsc.exe. This is consistent with RDP client use shortly after the addition, but does not identify a destination or demonstrate a successful remote session.

The explicitly recorded successful RDP session to FILE-RB-01 was dev.sharma connecting from WS-DSHARMA-01 at 10.60.10.23, not cole.price. That session does not establish use of cole.price's new membership.

known_telemetry_limitations: The alerted membership event identifies the subject account and logon session but contains no initiating process, command, ticket reference, or human-operator attribution (S27-00047, S27-00048).
The UserAssist event contains binary data without decoded execution details; it is not a destination-side authentication record and cannot establish successful RDP access (S27-00060).
The available address comparison distinguishes 10.60.10.22 from the observed WS-DSHARMA-01 address, but supplies no authoritative hostname mapping for 10.60.10.22 (S27-00047, S27-00052).
claims_not_established: Whether the addition was malicious, an administrative mistake, or an approved exception to the supplied policy is not established by the membership event (S27-00048).
Whether dev.sharma personally performed the change or the account was misused is not established by the matching authentication and membership records (S27-00047, S27-00048).
Whether cole.price successfully accessed any remote system using the new membership is not established; the nearby UserAssist artifact supplies no destination or authentication outcome (S27-00060).
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the change ticket and independent confirmation from dev.sharma for the exact cole.price-to-Remote Desktop Users addition recorded in S27-00048; verify whether it was an error or explicitly authorized exception.
Resolve 10.60.10.22 at 13:40 UTC using DHCP, IPAM, or endpoint records, then collect initiating-process and authentication evidence for the DC session in S27-00047.
Collect RDP client execution details from WS-CPRICE-01 and destination-side authentication/session logs to determine the destination and outcome associated with the artifact in S27-00060.
Verify current membership and obtain subsequent membership-change records to determine whether the addition in S27-00048 persisted or was corrected.
